title: Sigil and Garden
premise: Edmund Ravensworth, a hedge-mage hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-outlawed city of Vellumgate, discovers his name in a century-old book of prophecies alongside tonight's date and a stranger named Isolde Vane. Hunted by the Ministry of Seals and guided by Isolde—a disgraced sigil-keeper—he learns he is the last heir of the Raven Covenant that once bound the mortal realm to the dying dragon-realms. Betrayal by his oldest friend, who sold him out for a Ministry seat, forces Edmund to choose between restoring his own stolen power or spending it to reforge the covenant. In the end, Edmund sacrifices his magic entirely, reigniting the last dragon-fire with his bloodline's sigil, while Isolde rebuilds the covenant as its new keeper—leaving Edmund ordinary, visible, and finally at home.
about_author: Rafael Kavanagh is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing illuminated manuscripts before turning to fiction full-time. He lives in a coastal town where he keeps an impractical garden and writes maps of places that do not exist.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Edmund sells a luck-charm to a nervous clerk, concealing the true magic beneath his wares. POV: Edmund. Establishes his careful invisibility, his loneliness, and the Ministry patrols that make small magics dangerous. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine—the sense that safety is a loan, not a possession.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: A bookseller friend shows Edmund a recovered prophecy book; tonight's date appears beside his true name and a stranger's. POV: Edmund. Shock curdles into fear as he realizes someone wrote his real name a century ago. Emotional beat: vertigo—the floor of his hidden life giving way.

chapters.title: Isolde Vane
chapters.summary: The prophecy's second name finds him first: Isolde, an exiled sigil-keeper, saves him from a Ministry snatch-squad. POV: Edmund, with a brief Isolde interlude. She reveals the Raven Covenant and his bloodline. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual distrust.

chapters.title: What the Ministry Keeps
chapters.summary: Edmund infiltrates the Ministry of Seals' archive with Isolde's help, seeking the covenant's original terms. POV: Edmund. He finds evidence the outlawing of magic was itself a theft—the Ministry hoards confiscated power. Emotional beat: righteous anger replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Knew
chapters.summary: Edmund confides in Corwin, his closest friend since childhood, testing loyalty against secrecy. POV: Edmund. Corwin's hesitation plants doubt; a Ministry seal glints on his coat. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by the first taste of betrayal.

chapters.title: Down the Root-Road
chapters.summary: Fleeing the city through a forgotten root-road, Edmund and Isolde cross into the borderlands where dragon-magic still faintly breathes. POV: alternating. They learn the covenant's breaking is why crops fail and fires gutter. Emotional beat: wonder reawakening after years of suppression.

chapters.title: The Guttering Hearth
chapters.summary: They reach the Emberhold, where the last dragon-fire burns low in a stone hearth tended by the ancient warden Brannoc. POV: Isolde. Brannoc tests Edmund's claim and finds his sigil scarred over—someone sealed his magic long ago. Emotional beat: grief for a self he never knew.

chapters.title: Scar Tissue
chapters.summary: Brannoc performs a painful unsealing; Edmund relives the night his mother hid him in Vellumgate. POV: Edmund, dreamlike flashbacks. His power returns raw and frightening. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration intertwined—power as both inheritance and wound.

chapters.title: Terms of the Old Bargain
chapters.summary: Reading the covenant's true text, they learn it demanded balance: mortal magic fed the dragons, dragon-fire blessed the land. The Ministry broke the exchange to hoard power. POV: Isolde. Emotional beat: clarity—the corruption of power framed as law.

chapters.title: Corwin's Choice
chapters.summary: Corwin arrives under Ministry orders but hesitates; Edmund offers him truth instead of arrest. POV: Corwin. Torn between ambition and love, he warns them of a coming purge—but cannot bring himself to defect fully. Emotional beat: tragedy of a good man split down the middle.

chapters.title: The Purge of Vellumgate
chapters.summary: Ministry sweepers burn the charm-quarter; Edmund watches his old life incinerated from the hills. POV: Edmund. Innocent charm-buyers are taken. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve—the cost of staying invisible too long.

chapters.title: Sigilcraft
chapters.summary: Isolde trains Edmund in covenant-sigils, but his power answers too eagerly, echoing the Ministry's hunger. POV: Edmund. He nearly harms her in practice. Emotional beat: fear of himself; power's seduction made intimate.

chapters.title: The Warden's Price
chapters.summary: Brannoc reveals reforging the covenant requires a life-bound sigil—one bearer gives up their magic forever. Both Edmund and Isolde quietly decide to be that bearer without telling the other. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tender, tragic symmetry of secret sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ministry of One
chapters.summary: The Minister herself, Lady Seraphel, intercepts them—she bears a stolen dragon-sigil and has been feeding on hoarded fire for decades. POV: Seraphel. She offers Edmund partnership: rule beside her, magic unlimited. Emotional beat: temptation offered with terrifying sincerity.

chapters.title: What Power Promised Me
chapters.summary: Edmund wavers; a dream of restored status, his mother alive, Vellumgate remade tempts him. POV: Edmund. Isolde's honesty about her own past failures anchors him. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—loyalty to people versus loyalty to power's promises.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Emberhold
chapters.summary: Corwin, coerced by Seraphel, leads Ministry forces to the Emberhold; Brannoc falls defending the hearth. POV: Corwin, then Edmund. The dragon-fire gutters to embers. Emotional beat: fury, heartbreak, and Corwin's horrified realization of what he's done.

chapters.title: Ashes and Names
chapters.summary: With hours left before the fire dies and both realms begin to unravel, Edmund forgives Corwin—not absolution, just truth—and sends him to rally the city's frightened charm-folk. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: grace extended without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: At the hearth, Edmund and Isolde discover each other's secret intent and argue bitterly—each refusing to let the other pay alone. POV: alternating. Seraphel attacks mid-rite. Emotional beat: love expressed as argument; stakes at their peak.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Climax: Edmund seizes the rite first, carving his bloodline sigil into the hearthstone, pouring all his magic into the fire as Seraphel's stolen sigil is torn from her. The dragon-fire roars back to full flame; she collapses into ash-dust and age. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: transcendence through loss.

chapters.title: Ordinary Hands
chapters.summary: Magic-less Edmund wakes in the Emberhold, unable to feel the realms anymore—and strangely light. Isolde, now covenant-keeper, grieves with him and stays. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: hollow ache giving way to unexpected peace.

chapters.title: Vellumgate, Unsealed
chapters.summary: Months later, the covenant's renewal dissolves the Ministry's monopoly; magic returns lawfully to Vellumgate. Corwin, penitent, helps rebuild the charm-quarter. POV: Corwin. Emotional beat: redemption earned slowly, community reborn.

chapters.title: The Mapmaker's Garden
chapters.summary: Edmund, now truly a cartographer, maps the reopened root-roads and plants a garden over the old archive. Isolde visits between keepings; their bond grows unhurried. POV: Edmund. Final beat: belonging found not in power, but in visibility, work, and chosen company.
